articles.title: In 2023, Joe Burrow bought a $7.5 million Ohio mansion; years later, his riverfront estate remains a standout purchase
articles.summary: Joe Burrow paid $7.5 million for a three-acre estate in Anderson Township, Ohio, in the summer of 2023.
articles.body: Joe Burrow paid $7.5 million for a three-acre estate in Anderson Township, Ohio, in the summer of 2023. It was the most expensive home sale in Hamilton County that year. The Bengals quarterback bought the 7,300-square-foot house, which looks out over the Ohio River, shortly after signing a five-year, $275 million extension. Reports say he did it quietly, a few months before a wrist injury ended his season in November. Three years later, the purchase still looks smart, and the reasons go well beyond the price.Why Joe Burrow’s $7.5 million Ohio mansion still stands outStart with the timing. Joe Burrow signed the richest deal in NFL history at that point, and a few weeks later he spent about 2.7 percent of it on a house. That is not wild spending for a player earning his money. Most athletes in his position buy fast, buy loud and often buy twice.Burrow did the opposite. He chose a property about 15 minutes from Paycor Stadium, near Coldstream Country Club, in a suburb he could actually live in. No flashy announcement followed. The sale only came to light because public records and a Realtor.com listing gave it away.That restraint is the real story. A $7.5 million home in Cincinnati’s east side buys far more land and privacy than the same money would in Los Angeles or Miami. Burrow got space, quiet and a short commute to work. For a quarterback who gets hit for a living, quiet counts.What you actually get for $7.5 million on the Ohio RiverThe numbers are solid. Reports describe a stucco house of about 7,300 square feet, built in 2016 on former horse farm land. The listing counts 12 rooms. Most accounts say four bedrooms, though a few outlets list five, so the exact layout is worth treating with caution.The setting matters more than the room count. The lot sits on three acres, with open fields, mature trees, a pond and a white wooden fence. The Ohio River bends in the distance. Large windows pull in the light, and the house is described as built with modern, energy-conscious features.Burrow also reportedly planned to add a pool house for extra privacy. That detail says plenty. He was not shopping for a trophy. He was shopping for a place to disappear into on a Tuesday off.Compare that with where he came from. His family home in Athens, Ohio, was bought in 2005 for roughly $240,000. The jump from that house to this one is large, but the thread is the same: stay in Ohio, keep it simple, keep people out.The tax bill that went down and the break-in that rattled the neighborhoodHere is the part most buyers at this level would love. According to the Cincinnati Enquirer, property taxes on the estate fell after county valuations lowered its assessed value. The newspaper also noted that Burrow handled the market well, landing a deal on a home of this size. A record sale price and a smaller tax bill is an unusual pairing.The calm did not last. On a Monday night in December 2024, while Burrow was in Dallas helping Cincinnati to a 27-20 win, someone broke into the house. A person who works for him arrived to find a shattered bedroom window and a home in disarray, then called 911.Police arrested four men in January 2025 after a traffic stop. Authorities said they found items believed to be taken from Burrow’s home, and the group was tied to a string of burglaries at high-value properties across Ohio. Reports described the suspects as Chilean nationals, and the case moved through the local courts afterward.Burrow’s home was not special in that sense. Several NFL stars, including Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, have dealt with similar break-ins. The lesson for any athlete is blunt: a quiet address helps, but it does not replace real security, especially when your schedule is public and your games are on national television.Why Burrow keeps his money close to CincinnatiLook at the bigger picture and the house makes more sense. Burrow grew up in Ohio, played at Ohio State before transferring to LSU, and has spent his whole pro career with the Bengals. Putting millions into a home near the stadium sends a clear message about where he plans to be.The money side is easy to follow, too. His extension runs through 2028, with earnings climbing each year, and endorsements add several million more. Real estate in a market like Cincinnati holds value well, and a large lot near the river is not something developers can easily replace. If Burrow ever sells, the land alone gives buyers a reason to pay.There is also the human side that numbers miss. Burrow has had a rough few years health-wise, with the wrist injury in 2023 and other setbacks since. A house that lets a player recover in private, away from crowds, is worth more to him than an extra bedroom or a nicer pool.So does the purchase still hold up? On price, privacy and location, yes. The break-in showed the risks that come with fame, but it did not change the basic logic. Burrow bought a place to live rather than a place to be seen, and that choice has aged better than most splashy athlete purchases.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “A deal could happen at any time": Tyreek Hill's NFL comeback faces major hurdle as teams assess his recovery
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill could still become one of the most fascinating additions to an NFL roster this season.
articles.body: Tyreek Hill could still become one of the most fascinating additions to an NFL roster this season. With the playoff race heating up, teams searching for an offensive spark have a chance to explore a move that would require no trade negotiations. The former Miami Dolphins receiver remains a free agent, leaving the door open for any franchise interested in securing his services. However, his next move depends on more than just his reputation. After a serious knee injury disrupted his 2025 campaign, Hill faces an important challenge before he can return to the field.Tyreek Hill's free agency creates an opportunity for NFL contendersHill's availability presents an unusual opportunity for teams looking to strengthen their passing attacks before the postseason. At 32, the eight-time Pro Bowler still carries a reputation as one of the league's most dangerous deep threats. His speed can change the shape of a defence, even when he is not the primary target.Unlike a player involved in trade discussions, Hill can negotiate directly with any interested franchise. That means teams would not need to surrender valuable draft picks to bring him aboard. For organisations with Super Bowl ambitions, that could make the potential signing particularly attractive.However, his free-agent status does not guarantee an immediate return. Teams must consider whether he can deliver the same explosive performances that made him such a difficult matchup throughout his career.Tyreek Hill's knee recovery remains the biggest obstacle to an NFL returnThe biggest question surrounding Hill is his physical condition. His 2025 season ended in devastating fashion after he suffered a serious left knee injury during Week 4 with Miami. The injury involved a dislocation and multiple torn ligaments, requiring two major surgical procedures.Recovering from such damage takes time, particularly for a receiver whose greatest weapon is his ability to accelerate and create separation. Teams will want more than encouraging rehabilitation reports before making a financial commitment.Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has continued to signal that a return remains possible. He previously indicated that “a deal could happen at any time”. Still, interested teams are expected to seek complete medical clearance and assess his condition through private workouts.That cautious approach also explains why franchises have explored other receiver options, including Brian Thomas Jr. and Josh Downs, as the November 3 trade deadline approaches.For Hill, the coming weeks could prove decisive. His experience and game-changing ability make him an appealing option, but his recovery must match his ambition. Until teams receive convincing medical assurances, his NFL comeback will remain a possibility rather than a certainty.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “He needs to be fired”: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid backs Harrison Butker sparking major outrage ahead of clash against the New York Jets
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are reeling from two difficult back to back losses in the new season which seems to have made things difficult for the team in the
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs are reeling from two difficult back to back losses in the new season which seems to have made things difficult for the team in the new season. While all eyes remain on the team for the clash against the New York Jets, the Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid has defended Harrison Butker.Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid makes his stance clear on kicker Harrison Butker after the loss against the Denver BroncosA few hours ago, in an interview, the Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid weighed in on Harrison Butker’s performance at the game against the Denver Broncos as he said, “I could kind of see what he saw on that as far as he ended up going too far right…”The popular head coach said, “But I see why he went right too. We never talk about the protection on that and the overloads on that, but you have a heavy overload on the left side and penetration there.”The Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid continued, “That’s going to alter a kicker. I mean, that’s just what you do as a kicker. It’s no different than what quarterbacks do when they’re throwing the football. So sometimes you have to alter the alignment there. So I get it. It just went a little bit too wide on it. But we’ve got to do a better job of that, of the protection for him.” Reid added: “He kind of had to kick it that way to avoid being blocked.”Andy Reid’s comments sparks a heated debate about Harrison ButkerAndy Reid’s comments about Harrison Butker have now sparked a heated debate as fans have accused him of “protecting” the star kicker.A fan took to X and wrote, “Please ask Andy what has been discussed with Toub regarding Butker’s FG (distance, conditions, situations, etc)? Butker is 33.3% (2 of 6) in 2026 for that range before missing in Denver. Why attempt a 54 yard FG in that situation & conditions with someone only making 33.3%?”Another fan posted, “Even if true (which it’s not) he still fkn missed… stop making bad excuses for the kicker that has the most misses in the league.”A third fan wrote, “I’ve lost so much respect for Andy Reid for keeping him on the roster for this long. Do the right thing Andy. Release him.”However, neither the Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid nor the star player Harrison Butker has responded to the criticisms they are facing.For the unversed, Harrison Butker made a 31 yard field goal, converted a 45 yard field goal to close out the first half, and made all three of his extra point attempts.Later, in the fourth quarter, with the Chiefs trailing, Harrison Butker missed a wide-right 54-yard field goal attempt that would have given Kansas City a 28–27 lead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “The first time he struck my stomach”: Tyreek Hill’s estranged wife Keeta Vaccaro broke down in court amid their bitter legal battle
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, is yet to get back to the field after he sustained severe injuries in the last season when he was
articles.body: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, is yet to get back to the field after he sustained severe injuries in the last season when he was spotted visibly groaning in pain. Since then, life seems to have turned messier for the star wide receiver. A team has yet to sign him and he recently fought a tough legal battle against his estranged wife, Keeta Vaccaro.Tyreek Hill’s estranged wife Keeta Vaccaro became emotional at court as she fought against himA few weeks ago, as per New York Post, Tyreek Hill’s now estranged wife Keeta Vaccaro stood at the podium at court, visibly fighting back tears as she said, “The first time he struck at my stomach and punched it and I saved myself…”The popular entrepreneur Keeta Vaccaro added, “He was like, ‘I don’t want the baby.’”What really happened between Tyreek Hill and Keeta Vaccaro that ended their marriage in just a few months?For the unversed, Tyreek Hill and Keeta Vaccaro tied the knot in 2024, just months after the star player welcomed his ninth child with a different woman.Though there had been a lot of drama in Tyreek Hill’s personal life, he and Keeta Vaccaro seemed deeply in love with one another as she often showed up to cheer him on.But their marriage hardly lasted a few months, as last year, authorities were called to their rented place in Miami. Though no charges were filed against either of them, just a day later, Keeta Vaccaro filed for divorce and accused Tyreek Hill of brutal domestic violence.Following a high profile trial presided over by Judge Spencer Eig, the jury ordered the star player Tyreek Hill to pay his estranged wife Keeta Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages as he has expressed satisfaction.Despite the mess in his personal life, the former Miami Dolphins’ star wide receiver bounced back on the field but ended up with severe injuries.A few weeks ago, amid the controversial statements made by Tyreek Hill’s estranged wife, an NFL spokesperson said, “We have been monitoring developments in the matter, which remains under review of the personal conduct policy…”No action has been taken against the 32 year old free agent yet as Tyreek Hill is yet to land a new team, even though the season began two months ago.There have been serious concerns about Tyreek Hill’s full recovery as things remain uncertain.Though his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has spoken about the star wide receiver making a full recovery from is injuries, he recently visited Germany to seek more treatment.Coupled with his legal controversy, the future remains uncertain for Tyreek Hill now as he tries to stay out of the spotlight.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Ravens to start rookie Joe Fagnano at QB vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: The Jaguars will be going against the Ravens' third quarterback of the season.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens had hope before kickoff last Sunday. Ahead of their kickoff on Thursday, most of that hope has vanished with two months left in the season.

The Ravens suffered not one but two quarterback injuries on Sunday. Lamar Jackson dislocated his right thumb on his first play back from an ankle injury, then Tyler Huntley injured his toe. Both players are on injured reserve.

Before last Sunday, you would have had to have watched a lot of preseason football to know Joe Fagnano was the Ravens' third-string quarterback. The undrafted rookie is now elevated to QB1 for their game on Thursday night against a very good Jacksonville Jaguars team. There is help on the way next week, as the Ravens reportedly were finalizing a deal for Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but Fagnano will get at least one start.

Fagnano started his college career as a walk-on at Maine. He went to UConn after that and had an impressive 28-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio for the Huskies. He still went undrafted and signed with the Ravens with no money guaranteed. In his first NFL action last week, he completed 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards. He will benefit from getting starter's reps in practice, even though it's a short week. It's still a very tough assignment.

The Jaguars are 5-2 and lead the NFL with a +85 point differential. They're up to No. 2 in DVOA behind the 49ers and are the only team that ranks in the top-five of offense, defense and special teams in DVOA. Three of their five wins have come by 24 or more points. It looks like they'll run away with the AFC South.

The Ravens are just trying to stay alive in case Jackson can make a return sometime late in the season. They have to wait one more week for Brissett to be the bridge quarterback to that. This week, they're relying on an undrafted rookie to help pull off an improbable win.

It's reasonable to say the Ravens. If they win they'll be 5-4 with Jacoby Brissett coming on board. The season wouldn't technically be over at that point. However, Baltimore's chances of staying afloat over the second half of the season and also having Lamar Jackson return are slim. When you lose a two-time MVP quarterback to injured reserve, there's not much you can do about it. The Jaguars are cruising along at 5-2 and look like a legitimate Super Bowl contender. They might not be the more desperate team, but they're the one with a bright future this season. They need it more just because a loss to a reeling team with an undrafted rookie quarterback would poor cold water on the idea that the Jaguars can win a championship.

If the Ravens can pull off an upset, it will be because the defense plays great and the offense carries its quarterback. That formula puts a lot of pressure on Henry. It won't be easy against a Jaguars team that will likely come in not respecting the Ravens' passing game with a rookie making his first start. The Jaguars also allow the fewest rushing yards and rushing yards per carry in the NFL. That did come with defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton having a good season, and he suffered a season-ending quad injury last week. Henry had a good start to the season, but has had some quiet games lately with the Ravens suffering through bad quarterback play. He has 156 yards on 45 carries (3.5-yard average) over the last three weeks, and Baltimore hasn't scored more than 13 points in any of those games. But they need Henry to have a dominant performance Thursday, and that won't be easy against a good Jaguars defense.

The Jaguars travel to Baltimore to take on the M.A.S.H. unit that is the Ravens' remaining roster on Thursday night. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley? Both out on IR. Third-stringer Joe Fagnano will start, but is dealing with an ankle injury. Baltimore is reportedly trading for Jacoby Brissett, but he won't be playing this week. To put a little context into the state of both teams, this line was Ravens -4.5 this offseason, it re-opened Ravens +8 on Sunday and got as high as +10. The Jaguars are only 4-3 against the spread this season, but they're coming off a 42-7 rout of an undermanned Colts team. Baltimore has talent on both sides of the ball, but this is a big ask for Fagnano — on a short week and with an injury no less. There are some Jacksonville -9.5s out there in the market. I'd jump on one of those or put Jacksonville in a 7-point tease with the 49ers -9.5 to get both under a field goal. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Jacksonville at Baltimore looked like a signature game when the schedule was released, but all bets are off with Lamar Jackson unavailable. Here are three fantasy angles to track as you watch the game.

1. Can Zay Flowers survive? Flowers has shown the ability to produce with backups before — he was just fine with Tyler Huntley last year. But with Jackson and Huntley both unavailable and Jacoby Brissett a week away, the Ravens have to make do with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano in this spot. Flowers did not have a catch in the loss to Buffalo.

2. What does the Jacksonville pass distribution look like? Although Trevor Lawrence attempted just 14 passes last week, he found a way to target eight different players. Parker Washington is the unquestioned No. 1 receiver in the Jacksonville huddle, but we'd like to see him draw a larger market share.

3. Will Derrick Henry find running lanes? Henry is finally showing some attrition near the end of his Hall of Fame career, sliding down to 4.0 YPC. The loss of Jackson obviously doesn't help, and he'll be challenged by a Jaguars defense that's No. 1 in run defense DVOA. The Ravens would like to give Henry 20 or more touches, and attempt to shorten the game. — Scott Pianowski

Check out more of Scott's work at the Yahoo Sports fantasy hub .

articles.title: Mike Vrabel's Tom Brady reunion comes with a hilarious twist as Patriots coach jokes about contractual obligation
articles.summary: Mike Vrabel's return to New England has brought plenty of familiar faces back into his orbit, but a reunion with Tom Brady comes with an amusing catch.
articles.body: Mike Vrabel's return to New England has brought plenty of familiar faces back into his orbit, but a reunion with Tom Brady comes with an amusing catch. Ahead of the Patriots' reunion plans, Vrabel joked about his obligation to meet the franchise legend, turning what could have been a routine meeting into a lighthearted moment. The exchange also offers a glimpse into the relationship between two figures whose careers remain closely tied to the Patriots' most successful era.Mike Vrabel finds a funny way to describe his Tom Brady reunionMike Vrabel knows what Tom Brady means to the New England Patriots. The two shared the field during one of the most successful periods in franchise history, helping establish a winning culture that defined the organization for nearly two decades.Now, with Vrabel leading the Patriots as head coach, their paths are crossing again. However, his latest comment about meeting Brady added a little humor to the occasion.Rather than making the reunion sound like a major ceremonial moment, Vrabel joked about having a contractual obligation to meet the former quarterback. The remark brought a lighter side to the situation and showed the comfort he has with the people who helped shape his playing career.There is also a deeper connection behind the joke. Vrabel was part of the Patriots' dynasty as a linebacker, while Brady became the central figure of their championship run. They experienced the same demanding environment under Bill Belichick, where preparation, discipline and accountability were expected every day.Their relationship is therefore built on more than shared memories. Both understand what it took to keep New England competitive year after year. Vrabel's return as head coach also gives him a different perspective on the same organization he once helped lead on the field.Brady and Vrabel share a connection that goes beyond New England's dynastyBrady's legacy in New England is difficult to separate from the people who helped build the team's success. Vrabel was one of those players. His contributions on defense played an important role in the Patriots' championship years, and his experience alongside Brady gives their reunion a natural familiarity.But their roles have changed considerably since those playing days. Brady has moved into his post-playing career, while Vrabel now carries the responsibility of guiding a franchise that wants to return to its former standards.That makes the meeting interesting beyond the humorous contractual obligation comment. Brady represents the level of success New England once enjoyed, while Vrabel is tasked with creating a new version of it.There is no need to suggest that one conversation will change the Patriots' direction. Still, having two people with such a strong understanding of the franchise reconnect is a reminder of the standards that once made the organization so difficult to beat.For Vrabel, the reunion also brings a chance to reconnect with someone who experienced the same highs and pressures of playing in New England. And if his joke is any indication, the meeting is unlikely to be short on familiar banter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New Rumor Suggests NY Giants Being Forced To Wait on Jonathan Taylor Trade Until Specific Date
articles.summary: If the New York Giants are able to complete a blockbuster trade for Jonathan Taylor, a new report suggests it […]
articles.body:
If the New York Giants are able to complete a blockbuster trade for Jonathan Taylor , a new report suggests it will have to wait until just before next week's NFL trade deadline.

This will be an interesting next few days for the Giants. Heading into Sunday's NFL schedule, they own a 4-2-1 record and sit atop the NFC East standings. A year ago, they were 2-5 and considered potential sellers before the deadline. Now they can have reasons to shop for upgrades to make a serious run at the division title in the second half.

The word around the team is that improving the running back room is one of the front office's priorities before Nov. 10. And according to reports over the weekend, the Giants are competing with teams like the Minnesota Vikings and Denver Broncos in the ongoing Taylor sweepstakes.

In a trade deadline report this week, ESPN's Dan Graziano boldly claimed, "I would guess [Taylor] gets traded, and I wouldn't be at all surprised if it was the Giants who made that move ." That is certainly a promising view on Big Blue's chances of acquiring the three-time Pro Bowler. However, if New York can get the deal across the finish line, it won't happen until next week.

Indianapolis Colts holding off on Jonathan Taylor trade until right before the Nov. 10 deadline

"The belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday's game vs. the Dallas Cowboys before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday ahead of the deadline," Jordan Schultz reports.

Reports over the last couple of weeks suggest the Indianapolis Colts want a second-round pick and more in a trade for Taylor. That price could go up if teams are desperate enough to add the 27-year-old still under contract for two more seasons .

According to a previous report from Schultz, a major hurdle for New York to make trades before the deadline is " that the Giants don't have a 4th- or 5th-round pick in 2027 ." They gave up their fifth-rounder in September's JJ McCarthy trade, and their fourth in a deal with the Cleveland Browns last year.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Joel Smyth offers FLEX lineup advice for Quinshon Judkins, Raiders RBs, more players in Week 9
articles.summary: Joel Smyth helps you through those tough flex decisions for your Week 9 fantasy football lineups.
articles.body:
We're on to Week 9 of the fantasy football season! As we look for every advantage this season, the X-Factor position is the FLEX. To break it all down, Yahoo analyst Joel Smyth goes through 8 players in the consensus rankings flex zone for your flexes, double flexes or even third WR slots.

It's time. Jonah Coleman completely took over the backfield in Week 8, handling 11-of-13 carries after J.K. Dobbins opened with the first five. He had five targets, six opportunities at the goal line and a big fantasy day versus a top RB defense. The Panthers, on the other end, just fired their defensive coordinator. Denver, despite a slow start, ranks 10th in RB fantasy points in the first half of the season. With no RJ Harvey, plenty of valuable touches are available to the rookie in a great situation as a whole. Coleman has been the far more successful back and should be treated like such this weekend.

Miami is top-five against wide receivers this season and its passing defense has been terrible. On a per-play basis, the Dolphins rank dead last; they just have not been thrown on much this season. Williams isn't volume dependent, and he may need to hit early on versus the Dolphins to hit at all, but Miami's improvement on offense, paired with the Lions defense, can help.

Over the last month, Miami ranks 14th in scoring offense, which hopefully can keep it close to the powerhouse that is Detroit's offense, entering as touchdown underdogs. Williams' targets aren't always consistent or high, but they have been valuable downfield shots and in the red zone in a top offense, making the overall volume much closer to that of a fantasy WR2 over the last month. He's become a weekly set-and-forget with his production as of late.

With Dylan Sampson back, Judkins becomes much more game-script dependent. That game script has a better shot of staying in his favor this week as 2.5-point underdogs to New Orleans, hopefully a closer game than the 21-point loss to Pittsburgh last weekend. In the Browns' five wins this season, Judkins has scored 14.4 half-PPR PPG, handling an extreme share of the backfield carries and all the goal-line work. The Saints have been an RB's dream so far in 2026, ranking 32nd versus backs on the season, only getting worse over the last five games.​

The Jeanty experience has not been for the faint of heart. What we don't know is how this backfield will be split on the ground this week, the Raiders potentially sticking with Mike Washington Jr. completely, going back to 50-50 or (unlikely) swinging all the way back to Jeanty as the workhorse. What we do know is that there is a 90% chance Jeanty is the receiving back, something that alone would make him the RB22 in PPR scoring, as he's scored the most receiving fantasy points at the position. We also know that, although the 49ers have been the best defense in the NFL versus rushing fantasy points, they also rank 32nd against RB receiving points. I'm not confident if he's my RB1 or RB2, but I still believe he's worthy of a flex spot.​

Maybe give one more week for Odunze. This week I had a personal favorite come out with the Heaven versus Hell Graph , comparing the first half of the season schedule to the second half. Odunze is where you'd want with a much better schedule going forward… after this week. From Weeks 10-17, there isn't a spot you're scared of, but Week 9's matchup versus Tampa Bay isn't ideal.

Odunze will matchup versus Zyon McCollum on nearly half of the plays this Sunday. He's allowing a very low amount of production when targeted against to begin with. The Bucs' defense had been dominant against the pass long before Week 8 versus Atlanta, ranking No. 1 (over Minnesota!) in EPA/pass on the season.

It's been a rollercoaster for Pitts managers; what's new? This week, hopefully it's a game where you don't regret putting him in your lineup the next morning. There's a couple of main reasons why I think Pitts can be used as the extra flex. No. 1, the Bengals. They were horrible against tight ends last year, and are only a little better this season, giving up on average 5.3 PPG more than the average defense does to the position. They struggle up the middle in general and often find themselves in shootouts.

No. 2 is that Cincinnati plays a high amount of man coverage. Pitts is the seventh-best in fantasy points per route this season if he were a WR. For the second straight season, QB Michael Penix Jr. and Pitts have been best buds against man coverage, being the primary reason for most big Pitts days. You won't even need coffee Sunday morning for this game abroad if your heart is already racing with Pitts in the starting lineup.

The stat breaking down the 49ers' running back defense is why Washington is in the booby traps. San Francisco is 32nd versus receiving backs, but first against rushing, where Washington has an extremely low percent (10.8%) of his fantasy points from. If Washington does get the volume again, well, there's a good chance it doesn't work out anyway. The Raiders have converted two of their 17 goal-line carries, which is likely what it would take to overcome the 49ers' rushing defense. The floor is very low for multiple reasons, making it a pass for me until we have more knowledge of the split or at least a better matchup.

Arizona has shockingly not been a positive matchup for running backs this season. The defense is getting scored on more than any team in the NFL, yet they are second-best against RB fantasy points adjusted to the schedule. Charbonnet is coming off of a major injury with multiple other RB options available.

In Week 8, he only played 20-of-57 snaps on offense. It's not enough for me to trust, with around 10 touches being the expected volume. In the past, spots such as these could be salvaged with the goal-line touchdown, which certainly can happen, but a lower shot with the red-zone work being split three ways last week. It's not a guarantee the goal-line carry goes to Charbonnet if there is one at all.
